title: Spuriosity Rankings: Sorting Data to Measure and Mitigate Biases

bias_targets.methodology: Ranking images within classes based on 'spuriosity' (the presence of spurious cues proxied via robust neural feature activations) and measuring the 'spurious gap', defined as the drop in model accuracy between high and low spuriosity images across datasets like ImageNet and Waterbirds.

Using a lightweight robust feature discovery framework to identify race-related spurious correlations (e.g., associating brown skin with brown hair in Celeb-A, or associating glasses with the Indian race class in UTKFace) and visually analyzing the top and bottom activating images.

Applying the robust neural feature framework to gender classification tasks (e.g., UTKFace) to uncover gender-related spurious features, such as associating suits/ties with the male class and the color pink with the female class, by sorting instances based on feature activation.
